metric.why: Capex is the audited ground truth beneath every buildout headline. This site reads it directly from EDGAR company facts, quarterly, for the hyperscalers and the largest colocation operators.
metric.definition: Quarterly capital spending reported to the SEC by the companies building the facilities, tracked on this page from each company's own XBRL filings.

reading.body:
Hyperscaler and colocation operators' quarterly capital expenditure, reported directly to the SEC, is the most reliable measure of how fast the physical infrastructure for AI is actually scaling.

Companies building data centers must report capex to investors every quarter. This creates an audited record independent of marketing claims or strategic announcements. The spending patterns here show which facilities are under construction, which are expanding, and how urgently. For AI specifically, capex is the constraint that matters most. Compute exists only in buildings. Buildings require power and space. The speed at which capex grows or shrinks directly limits how many GPUs can be deployed in the next six to eighteen months.

This data does not reveal utilization rates, power efficiency, or how much of the capex goes to AI workloads versus other services like traditional cloud computing or storage. It also does not cover smaller operators or private companies that do not file with the SEC. The data measures spending commitment, not completion. A large capex quarter signals intent to build, but the building itself takes time and can face delays in power delivery, permitting, or equipment procurement.
